newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Akzo to deconsolidate Dfl 1 bn in turnover.
newsitem.headline: Akzo to deconsolidate Dfl 1 bn in turnover.

text.p: Chemicals group Akzo Nobel said on Thursday it planned to deconsolidate some one billion guilders' worth of turnover in 1997 as part of a drive to hive off non-core businesses.

"Deconsolidations will include Salt America, for which the contract has been signed subject to regulatory approval, ROVIN (Akzo's joint venture with Shell for VCM and PVC) and Delamine," Akzo chairman Cornelis van Lede told a results news conference.
Akzo signed an agreement with commodities giant Cargill in August last year to sell off its U.S. salt activities after earlier closing down its Retsof salt mine.
Board member Rudy van der Meer stressed that the ROVIN and Delamine deconsolidations amounted to paper transactions.
"These two will operate as independent deconsolidated joint ventures in which Akzo will retain a 50 percent stake," Van der Meer said.
Finance director Jean den Hoed said Delamine, an Akzo joint venture with Tosoh of Japan, would be deconsolidated as Tosoh had become more of a rival since the Akzo-Nobel merger in 1993.
As a result of the merger Akzo acquired Nobel's ethylene amines activities in Stenungsund, Sweden.
An attempt to group Tosoh's and Akzo Nobel's global ethylene amines activities under a single umbrella proved unsuccessful, so Akzo had to deconsolidate, Van der Meer said.
"Stenungsund is a fully-functioning facility, in which we have recently made considerable investments and which is looking to Asia," Van der Meer said.
Van Lede said on Thursday that the sell-off of Salt America to Cargill did not mean Akzo was also seeking to divest Salt Europe.
"The American salt activities are of a completely different nature -- they are only active in de-icing," he said.
By contrast Salt Europe produced salt for chemical conversion, industrial applications and consumer uses, he said.
Asked about the company's acquisition plans, Van Lede said Akzo's favourable financial position gave it plenty of leeway for new buys.
But he declined to give any details of planned acquisitions beyond saying that Akzo was looking for takeover candidates in the high-margin sectors of pharmaceuticals and coatings.
Akzo said earlier it expected to post increased profits in 1997 on the back of turnover roughly unchanged from 1996.
The company reported 1996 turnover of 22.44 billion guilders, up from 21.49 billion in 1995.
-- Lien van der Leij, Amsterdam newsroom +31 20 504-5000
